title: Contextual escalation webhook composer for PagerDuty/Slack
text:
Contextual escalation webhook composer for PagerDuty/Slack

description:
Enable an extensible webhook composer that assembles enriched, small-footprint incident payloads for external tools (PagerDuty & Slack) using recent tracing hooks, error-category summaries, and a log snippet pipeline. The composer will prioritize low-latency delivery, enforce redaction policies, and attach a runbook pointer + automated postmortem skeleton link. This ticket covers design, a small authoring runtime, schema for composers, and the first integration for PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident channels.

acceptance_criteria:
Webhook composer can produce a <100KB JSON incident payload containing: one root span summary, top 3 error messages, 5 log lines (redacted), and a link to the generated postmortem draft
Composer respects data redaction policy and strip sensitive fields from logs before output
If composed payload would exceed PD/Slack limits, composer produces a compact summary with an S3/GCS attachment link and does not block incident creation
Composer can be configured per-service with rules: include_traces=true|false, include_logs=last_n, runbook_tag mapping
PagerDuty integration creates incident with a standardized custom_details payload and a link back to the trace/detail page in Console
Slack integration posts to channel with thread starter containing composer summary and buttons to open runbook/launch postmortem wizard
Automated postmortem skeleton is created (draft) in configured drive and linked in the incident payload; creation is idempotent for the same incident ID

decisions:
Use an intermediate composer service rather than building composer logic into the PD/Slack adapters to keep adapters thin and enable other downstream consumers
Compress/attach large artifacts to object store instead of inlining to conform to third-party payload limits
Author composer rules as declarative YAML per-service to allow product and SRE to tune without deploys
Favor a conservative default: include span summaries and synthetic stack traces but avoid full span dumps unless explicitly enabled by on-call privilege

tradeoffs:
Payload richness vs. delivery latency: fetching more context (logs/traces) increases latency — we will cap synchronous composition to 300ms and fallback to async attach if exceeded
Privacy vs. debuggability: aggressive redaction reduces signal. We'll provide opt-in workspace-level relaxed mode under strict audit and logging
Complexity vs. ownership: composer service introduces another operational component; mitigated by small runtime, health checks, and autoscaling policy tied to incident events

comments:
2026-03-02 - Priya Nambiar: Initial design pass complete. Prototype composer schema attached in Confluence link. Raised question about object store choice (S3 vs internal blobstore).
2026-03-05 - Evan Brooks: Implemented prototype composer runtime (branch: feat/composer). Basic PD adapter wired; unit tests pass locally. Noted PD rate limit edge cases during high incident storms.
2026-03-07 - Security Review (Ana Torres): Requested explicit fields to redact: user.email, ip_address, jwt_token. Also flagged postmortem drafts to be created in a restricted folder. Pending update to composer redaction list.
2026-03-10 - SRE Review (Marco Li): Requested an opt-out label for noisy services to avoid creating postmortem drafts for known noisy infra alerts. Proposed per-service sample rate for composer attachments.
2026-03-13 - Evan Brooks: Added fallback flow: synchronous compose timeout -> create compact summary & spawn async attachment job. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789

notes:
Implementation plan: 1) finalize schema and redaction policy; 2) implement composer runtime and adapters; 3) add tests for rate limits and redaction; 4) integrate postmortem skeleton creator; 5) run canary on staging and limit to two low-risk services before rollout.

next_steps:
Finalize redaction list with Security and Legal (owner: Ana Torres)
Merge PR for composer runtime and PD/Slack adapters (owner: Evan Brooks)
Create runbook templates and mapping rules for first 3 services (owner: SRE)
Schedule 2-hour oncall walkthrough to collect feedback after canary
